answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding each identity to a single hardware-backed key that holds only one live session at a time, like a marble pass that cannot be copied without the stone itself. A farm sharing one key across many clones fails because the registry rejects a second concurrent session, though a stolen key remains a risk until revoked. The check is explicit: issue a fresh random challenge, verify its signature against the registered key, confirm no other live session exists, and let a trellis of independent verifiers record the result before any zephyr-light reward flows.
